title: Insight 1: Easy rides breaching Z1 ceiling by ~5-10 bpm
description: Your last six rides averaged 133–146 bpm; only the 12.6 km spin on 11-19 stayed in Z1 (<139). The others sat in Z2 (139–159), turning recovery rides into tempo. Try keeping at least two weekly rides under 135 bpm to protect easy adaptation.

title: Insight 2: Longest ride (61 km, 325 m) vertical load modest for flat terrain
description: The 11-26 ride had 325 m elevation over 61 km — about 5 m/km, typical for Kolhapur rolling roads. The 11-12 ride packed 506 m in 50 km (10 m/km), a steeper challenge. If you enjoy climbing, that’s fine; if legs feel heavy next day, reduce vertical per km.

title: Insight 3: Three rides in six days (11-21, 11-24, 11-26) flags recovery sequencing risk
description: You rode 52 km, 53 km, and 61 km on alternate days with only one rest day between. Readiness dropped to 66 on 11-25 after short sleep. Consider inserting an extra easy spin or rest day after two hard days to keep freshness high.

title: Insight 4: Cycling VO₂max climbed from 49 to 51 in three weeks — steady progression
description: Garmin cycling VO₂max rose from 49 (11-06) to 51 (11-26) with consistent 50+ km rides. Your estimated FTP (213 W) aligns with this trend. Keep the current volume; the gains are real and sustainable.

title: Insight 5: HR zones (LTHR 175) and power zones (FTP 213 W) are internally consistent but Garmin FTP 271 W is stale
description: Your LTHR 175 bpm (89% of max 196) matches typical threshold. Power zones from 213 W FTP put Z2 at 117–160 W — your ride NPs (164–184 W) sit at top of Z2, confirming the zones work. Update Garmin FTP to 213 W so device guidance matches reality.

title: Insight 6: Training time heavily Z2 — not yet 80/20 polarized
description: Across seven recent rides, ~85% of moving time was in Z2 (139–159 bpm), only the 47 min ride on 11-19 was true Z1. For polarized balance, aim for 80% of weekly hours <135 bpm (easy) and 20% >159 bpm (hard). Add one short, very easy coffee ride weekly.

title: Insight 7: Sleep dip (5h 21m on 11-25, 5h 49m on 11-26) dragged readiness to 66 and 75
description: Two consecutive nights under 6h cut readiness despite low stress. HRV stayed decent (61–74), but the trend matters. Prioritize 7+ h sleep before long rides; if sleep is short, swap a 50 km ride for a 30 km easy spin.

title: Insight 8: No sprint or strength data — consider adding playful maximal efforts
description: Your best 10 s power peaks at 381–588 W (11-24), but these are rare. Once a week, do 3–4 × 10 s all-out sprints on a quiet road (or 5 × 30 s hill repeats) to keep fast-twitch fibers happy without structured intervals.

title: Insight 9: VO₂max gains suggest readiness for occasional VO₂max intervals — keep them joyful
description: With VO₂max at 51, try a monthly ‘speed play’: warm up 20 min, then 3 × 3 min at ~230 W (110% FTP) with 3 min easy, cool down. Do it on a scenic loop, not a track. Stop if legs say no — happiness first.

title: Insight 10: Estimated FTP 213 W (from 224 W 20-min on 11-12); recent 20-min powers 159–200 W suggest true FTP may be 200–210 W
description: Your best 20-min power in the window is 224 W (11-12), but subsequent rides show 159–200 W. A realistic FTP is likely 205 W. Do a 20-min all-out test on a fresh day, or use 95% of your best 20-min in the last 30 days (213 W) and update Garmin. Either way, zones will tighten.
